rationale: A wins because it knows where the story stops and where the reporting has to begin. Its best line, “Patagonia has resold 500,000 used items — and won't say what resale is worth to it,” turns the disclosure gap into the story without pretending the company gave more than it did. B has useful bones, but “something no major apparel brand has attempted” and “designed to shorten its own sales pipeline” are exactly the kind of overconfident filler that gets a founder in trouble on the first reporter call.
gaps_in_A: “Only a company with no shareholders to please could give repairs away” overstates the ownership point; the supplied fact is private ownership and profits directed to environmental causes, not a proven monopoly on this behavior.
“triages it into free/at-cost/resale” implies a repair-to-resale routing system the update does not establish.
The business-model angle needs one harder caveat: Patagonia has not said repairs reduce new purchases, so do not pitch that as fact.
gaps_in_B: “something no major apparel brand has attempted” is an invented comparative claim. No competitor scan was supplied.
“at a scale no comparable US apparel brand has matched” repeats the same unsupported market-superlative problem.
“designed to shorten its own sales pipeline” assigns intent and business impact Patagonia did not state.
“The free jacket repair” invents a product example and implies the repair is free, when the facts say basic repairs are free and complex repairs are charged at cost.
